action.name: Installed-service padless HyperBoost low-power lifecycle validation
action.value: Balanced and Automatic to service-owned HyperBoost, one operator-initiated Windows sleep/resume boundary, then read-only lifecycle verification

validation.applyResult: Applied successfully once through the exact installed validation Service while the cooling pad was physically absent.
validation.readbackResult: Confirmed service-owned HyperBoost and a durable ownership journal before the low-power boundary.
validation.restorationResult: Failed lifecycle restoration: the service did not observe the required low-power lifecycle boundary and left HyperBoost active until a separate authorized typed cleanup.
validation.restorationReadbackResult: A later one-shot typed cleanup confirmed Balanced and Automatic; this cleanup does not validate automatic low-power restoration.

sanitizedEvidence.summary: The validation build bound the exact RZ09-0581 BIOS 4.00 installation, Balanced and Automatic baseline, admitted full-power adapter, confirmed physical pad absence, and a one-time validation manifest.
The installed Service applied HyperBoost once, confirmed mode 7, finalized durable ownership, and created the private marker without cleanup or manual recovery.

After the operator initiated Windows sleep for approximately ten seconds and resumed, the same Service instance remained active but no owned HyperBoost low-power recovery attempt or completion was recorded.
After the read-only failure result, one authorized typed Service cleanup restored and confirmed Balanced and Automatic without retry; a fresh read-only baseline then passed every safety check.
The private arm and verification records remain uncommitted; this annotation retains only bounded hashes, lengths, semantic outcomes, and exact executable provenance.

limitations: This is authoritative negative evidence for the tested low-power path: Windows display and power notifications did not reach the Service as the lifecycle boundary required by the recovery implementation.
The separate typed cleanup proves safe restoration after the failed validation, not automatic sleep/resume recovery.
Production padless HyperBoost must remain disabled while the low-power lifecycle gate is false.

productionAdmission.reason: The installed Service did not restore owned padless HyperBoost across the observed sleep/resume boundary.

notes: No Razer service was started, stopped, or restored.
Private lifecycle markers, diagnostics, local paths, and service instance identifiers are not committed.
